/// before Recording.
    func renderTools(ticks: String) -> [[String: Any]] {
        // `render_frame`'s three image containers, read off `FrameWriter`'s
        // own enum rather than restated, and hoisted for the type checker's
        // budget.
        let frameFormatNames = FrameWriter.Format.allCases.map { $0.rawValue }
        let frameFormatProperty: [String: Any] = [
            "type": "string", "enum": frameFormatNames,
            "description": "The container to write. Default: the path's own extension when it "
                + "is one of those (.jpg counts as jpeg), else png — so a call with no path "
                + "and no format writes a PNG, as it always has. An explicit format WINS and "
                + "the path's extension is REPLACED rather than appended to, so {path: "
                + "\"shot.jpg\", format: \"png\"} writes shot.png. png and heic keep the "
                + "canvas's alpha; \(FrameWriter.flattenNote)",
        ]
        // The burn-in argument, written ONCE and shared by `render_frame` and
        // `export`: the two are the same question about the same layer, and
        // two spellings of it would drift the first time either was edited.
        let burnInProperty: [String: Any] = [
            "type": "boolean",
            "description": "Draw the project timecode over the picture, topmost — the export "
                + "sheet's Burn in timecode checkbox. Default: false. It is a review copy's "
                + "reference, so it reads the DOCUMENT'S timecode in the document's own "
                + "spelling (the toolbar's, non-drop, HH:MM:SS:FF or HH:MM:SS.mmm), and it "
                + "shows PROJECT time even in a file written from the in/out range: a range "
                + "export starting at 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 carrying a burn-in that "
                + "reads 00:00:10:00, which is the number a note about that frame needs.",
        ]
        // `export`'s two alpha-bearing arguments, hoisted for the type checker's
        // budget and because both had to grow the same sentence.
        //
        // **A capability an agent cannot read is a capability it does not
        // have.** Phase 7b gave the table two rows that keep a transparent
        // canvas and gave `ExportWriter` a refusal for one of them, and
        // neither reached the schema — so the tool promised a letterbox where
        // the build throws, and the row to ask for was named nowhere a caller
        // could see it. There are four such rows since CX-17, and the refusal
        // is the MOVIE rows', `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha` and `vp9_alpha_webm`:
        // `apng` takes the ImageIO path, which FITS instead of padding.
        let exportPresetProperty: [String: Any] = [
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Export preset id — one per encoding, a container and a codec with "
                + "no size of its own (that is size's). h264 is what the export sheet opens "
                + "on. Four rows keep a transparent canvas transparent: prores_4444, "
                + "hevc_alpha and vp9_alpha_webm (the movie rows — see size, which constrains "
                + "them) and apng. "
                + "gif is not one of them: it can show a transparent pixel but has no alpha "
                + "channel, so nothing partial survives it. prores_422, prores_4444 and "
                + "hevc_10bit keep the compositor's 16-bit frames at 10 bits (ProRes 4444 at "
                + "12); h264, hevc and hevc_alpha are 8-bit. av1 is AV1 in an MP4 with AAC "
                + "and av1_webm the same AV1 in a WebM with Opus, both 10-bit, encoded by "
                + "the bundled SVT-AV1 at encoder_speed; Macs before M3 cannot play them "
                + "back. vp9_webm is VP9 in a WebM with Opus from the bundled libvpx, at "
                + "one speed: 8-bit (Profile 0) for an SDR picture, 10-bit (Profile 2) for "
                + "HLG and PQ. vp9_alpha_webm is that VP9 with its alpha, always 8-bit (the "
                + "SDR version in an HLG project), the transparent movie Chrome and Firefox "
                + "play; Safari's is hevc_alpha. Pass a wrong one and the error lists them all.",
        ]
        let exportSizeProperty: [String: Any] = [
            "type": ["string", "array"],
            "items": ["type": "integer"], "minItems": 2, "maxItems": 2,
            "description": "Output size — the sheet's Size popup. A row id: document (the "
                + "default, the document's own size, evened on the formats that need it), "
                + "1080p, 720p, 1440p or 2160p (the number is the SHORT edge and the long "
                + "edge follows the document's aspect, rounded to even, so a vertical "
                + "project's 1080p is 1080 × 1920), or preset for an "
                + "image format's cap (gif and apng, where it is the default) — or an explicit "
                + "[width, height] in px, the sheet's Custom…. Every row exists on every "
                + "document — a 1920 × 1080 project's 1080p is its own size and is listed "
                + "anyway — so an id means the same thing wherever it is sent; only preset is "
                + "confined to gif and apng. Omit for the document size or the image format's "
                + "cap; a wrong id's error lists the ids. A movie is written at exactly the "
                + "size asked for, letterboxed if the shape differs by more than a pixel "
                + "(within a pixel the picture fills the frame instead) — except on "
                + "prores_4444, hevc_alpha and vp9_alpha_webm, where a size of a DIFFERENT "
                + "SHAPE from the "
                + "canvas is refused rather than written, because the padding destroys the "
                + "alpha channel those rows are chosen for; every row id is already the "
                + "document's own shape, so this only bites on a [width, height] of another "
                + "shape. h264, hevc, hevc_alpha, hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, "
                + "vp9_alpha_webm and prores_422 need even dimensions: an odd width or height "
                + "— the document size on a canvas "
                + "with an odd edge, or an odd [width, height] — is written one pixel smaller "
                + "on that edge, and the width and height reported back are the file's. "
                + "The shape is judged on that even frame: a [width, height] in the canvas's "
                + "own proportions is never refused for being odd, at any scale; one of "
                + "another shape is judged as the even size it becomes, which is the size "
                + "hevc_alpha's refusal names. "
                + "prores_4444, gif and apng keep an odd edge. On gif and apng a size — the "
                + "cap, a row, or [width, height] — is a box the picture is fitted inside, aspect "
                + "kept and never upscaled, and the width and height reported back are the "
                + "file's: a vertical 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default is 152 × 270.",
        ]
        return [
            tool(
                "render_frame",
                "Renders one frame of the finished timeline as a picture so you can SEE the "
                    + "result — the verification hook. It goes through the same composition and "
                    + "the same Metal compositor an export does, so this is what the file will "
                    + "contain at that moment, not a preview of it. The image comes back both "
                    + "as an image block and as a file on disk whose path the text names. Use it "
                    + "before and after every edit. It writes a PNG to a temporary file unless "
                    + "path or format says otherwise, so a call that names neither is exactly "
                    + "the call it always was. When a graphic in the frame warned or failed, a "
                    + "sentence before the last names the graphic, its frame and the "
                    + "diagnostic; a failed graphic draws its error card in the picture. A "
                    + "media with a cursor file not in its picture (add_media's cursor) has its "
                    + "recorded cursor and click ripples drawn in its clips; when the file "
                    + "cannot be read the clip draws without one and a sentence says \"The "
                    + "cursor of media M is not drawn: <why>.\" A clip with set_video cutout "
                    + "waits up to 30 s for its masks (a picture with subject foreground, its "
                    + "foreground masks; any other, its person masks); past that it is drawn "
                    + "uncut and a sentence before the last names it. In an "
                    + "HLG project (set_canvas output) the frame is a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit "
                    + "HEIC labelled BT.2100 HLG; a JPEG, and any frame asked with "
                    + "sdr_version, is the project's SDR version, labelled BT.709. Its scopes "
                    + "read the picture it draws: in an HLG project the HLG signal, each JSON "
                    + "adding signal \"hlg\" and, for the waveform, parade and histogram, scale "
                    + "(the HLG % ticks in cd/m², reference white at 75 %), the luma and "
                    + "vectorscope taking Rec. 2020's weights and targets; the SDR version's "
                    + "scopes are an SDR project's.",
                [
                    "t": [
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "The moment to render, \(ticks) Default: the playhead.",
                    ],
                    "max_width": [
                        "type": "integer", "minimum": 16, "maximum": 8192,
                        "description": "Cap the image's width in px, aspect kept and never "
                            + "upscaled. Default: the canvas's own size.",
                    ],
                    "path": [
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Where to write the file, e.g. ~/Desktop/shot.png. The "
                            + "folder must exist. Omit for a temporary file; either way the "
                            + "text block's last sentence names the file that was written. "
                            + "This is the same writer File ▸ Save Frame… uses, so a PNG "
                            + "written here and one saved from the menu are byte-identical.",
                    ],
                    "format": frameFormatProperty,
                    "burn_in_timecode": burnInProperty,
                    "ungraded": [
                        "type": "boolean",
                        "description": "Render as if no clip were graded — every clip's "
                            + "video.color (Light and Color), video.wheels and video.curves "
                            + "neutral and no video.look: View ▸ Show Ungraded's picture. The view switch itself never "
                            + "reaches this tool or an export. Default false.",
                    ],
                    // View ▸ Show SDR Version's mirror (spec §11 HD-7, HD-14).
                    "sdr_version": [
                        "type": "boolean",
                        "description": "Draw an HDR (HLG) project's SDR version — what h264, "
                            + "hevc, hevc_alpha, gif, apng, JPEG frames and dynamic_range "
                            + "\"sdr\" write: the inverse of the lift, white titles near white, "
                            + "highlights above reference white rolled off. View ▸ Show SDR "
                            + "Version's picture; the switch itself never reaches this tool or "
                            + "an export. An SDR project's frame is its own SDR version, "
                            + "byte-identical. Default false.",
                    ],
                    "selection": [
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "An adjustment clip's id: draw what its video.qualifier "
                            + "selects instead of grading — grey, white fully graded, black "
                            + "untouched, its blurred selection when video.qualifier.blur is "
                            + "above 0, times any matte cutting it, its strength not applied "
                            + "— with every layer in front of it left out; black where the clip "
                            + "is not on the frame. View ▸ Show Selection's picture; the view "
                            + "switch itself never reaches this tool or an export. Refused "
                            + "unless it names an adjustment clip. Default: none.",
                    ],
                    "waveform": [
                        "type": "boolean",
                        "description": "Also measure the frame's luma waveform, View ▸ "
                            + "Scopes' Waveform: the text says what share of pixels clips high "
                            + "and low, and <image path>.waveform.json holds the 256 × 256 "
                            + "counts (one array per column bin, indexed by level), the clip "
                            + "marks and both percentages. Default false.",
                    ],
                    "parade": [
                        "type": "boolean",
                        "description": "Also measure the frame's RGB parade, View ▸ Scopes' "
                            + "Parade: R′, G′ and B′ each binned as the waveform bins Y′. The "
                            + "text says what share of pixels each channel clips high and low, "
                            + "and <image path>.parade.json holds the counts keyed red, green "
                            + "and blue (each 256 arrays by column bin, indexed by level) with "
                            + "each channel's clip marks and clip counts. Default false.",
                    ],
                    "vectorscope": [
                        "type": "boolean",
                        "description": "Also measure the frame's vectorscope, View ▸ Scopes' "
                            + "Vectorscope: Rec. 709 Cb and Cr of the encoded values in "
                            + "256 × 256 bins centred on neutral (bin 128). The text says what "
                            + "share of pixels is neutral, and <image path>.vectorscope.json "
                            + "holds the counts (256 arrays by Cr bin, indexed by Cb bin), the "
                            + "zoom, off_plot (the pixels left off the plot at a zoom, 0 at 1), "
                            + "the six 75 % targets' bins at the zoom (null off the plot) and the "
                            + "skin line's angle. Default false.",
                    ],
                    // A vectorscope slot's zoom cells, "1× 2× 4×" (spec §11 GR-31).
                    "vectorscope_zoom": [
                        "type": "integer", "enum": [1, 2, 4],
                        "description": "The vectorscope's zoom, as a vectorscope slot's 1× 2× "
                            + "4× cells: each pixel is binned 128 + round(255 × zoom × Cb) (and "
                            + "Cr), so ×2 and ×4 spread a near-grey picture over more bins; at "
                            + "2 and 4 a pixel off the plot is not counted and the text says "
                            + "what share lie off it. Needs vectorscope: true. Default 1.",
                    ],
                    "histogram": [
                        "type": "boolean",
                        "description": "Also measure the frame's histogram, View ▸ Scopes' "
                            + "Histogram: R′, G′, B′ and Y′ counts per 256 levels. The text says "
                            + "what share of pixels clips high and low by Y′, and <image "
                            + "path>.histogram.json holds the four planes' counts and both "
                            + "percentages. Default false.",
                    ],
                ]),
            tool(
                "export",
                "Starts writing the timeline to a file and answers AT ONCE with "
                    + "{export_id, path, status} — ⌘E, the export sheet's six controls (format, "
                    + "size, frame rate, quality, loudness, range) in the sheet's own "
                    + "vocabulary, all but the frame rate — this exports at the document's "
                    + "rate, or on gif and apng at the format's own rate (12.5 and 25 fps). The "
                    + "export is a job in the Export Queue, run one at a time behind any other "
                    + "export already there; status is queued or running. An av1, av1_webm "
                    + "or vp9_webm job also waits while the app's other AV1 and VP9 exports "
                    + "would hold more than a quarter of this Mac's memory with it, and a later "
                    + "job may run first meanwhile (export_status's waiting says so). Follow "
                    + "it with "
                    + "export_status, which never waits — call it again after a pause until "
                    + "status is done, failed or cancelled — and stop it with cancel_export. "

<class 'list'> 138
save_project
Saves the project. A project that has never been saved — a new_project with no path, or a movie opened as one — needs a path; passing a path always writes there (Save As). Returns once the package is really on disk. A path another open project holds is refused; close_project closes that one first.
{
"type": "object",
"properties": {
"path": {
"description": "Where to write the .framejob package. Required the first time; otherwise the project is written back to its own file.",
"type": "string"
},
"project": {
"type": "string",
"description": "Path of the open project to act on, as get_project reports it; omit for the frontmost one."
}
},
"required": []
}

get_project
The whole project as JSON: canvas (width, height, fps [num, den], background, fit_new_clips, timecode_frames), media, tracks, clips and markers, with next_id — the schema every op edits. Plus the state that is deliberately NOT in the model and lives only in the app: playhead, selection and the in/out range. Read this first: every other tool names things by the ids it reports, and clip, track, marker and media ids share ONE number space, so an id is unambiguous on its own. tracks[0] is the BACK of the layer stack (the bottom lane of the timeline); times are ticks at 600000 per second. missing_media lists media whose file has moved — relink_media points it at the new one. graphics: every module in the package's graphics/ with its revision, whether it compiles, and the clips drawn by it.
{
"type": "object",
"required": [],
"properties": {
"project": {
"type": "string",
"description": "Path of the open project to act on, as get_project reports it; omit for the frontmost one."
}
}
}

set_scope
Opens a nest so the app is LOOKING INSIDE it — double-clicking a nest clip in the timeline (Clip ▸ Open Nest, ⌘↓; Close Nest, ⌘↑). View state like the playhead and the selection: no op runs, nothing is undoable and the project is untouched. What it changes is what the app shows and therefore what get_project and render_frame answer — while a nest is open those report and draw that nest's own tracks, clips and frozen canvas rather than the timeline's, which is the only way to SEE what an edit inside one did. Name the nest, or the clip that shows it; call it with neither to come back out. While a nest is open every op you send lands INSIDE it unless the op's own scope argument says otherwise, exactly as an edit made by hand goes where the window is looking — so this is the setting to change first and the one to clear when you are done. Editing inside a nest does not require it: an op carrying scope works from wherever you are.
{
"required": [],
"type": "object",
"properties": {
"nest": {
"type": "integer",
"description": "The nest to open, by id (get_project lists them under nests). It has to be shown by a clip on the TIMELINE: this is the view, and the app cannot show its way into a nest the timeline does not reach — an op's own scope still can. Where two clips show one nest the earliest is entered, ties going to the lower id."
},
"clip": {
"type": "integer",
"description": "The nest CLIP to open — the precise spelling, and what a double-click sends: it names the nest and the start the times inside are measured from, which two clips showing one nest do not share. A clip that shows no nest is refused by name. Pass this or nest, not both."
},
"project": {
"type": "string",
"description": "Path of the open project to act on, as get_project reports it; omit for the frontmost one."
}
}
}

add_clip
Places a whole media file as one clip at `at` on `track` — dragging a Media-tab row onto a track. The clip starts at source time 0 and runs the media's whole length snapped DOWN to whole frames, so it never outruns the file; trim it afterwards with trim_start / trim_end. It is given Fit scale when the project's fit_new_clips is on and the source is bigger than the canvas. Refused when it would break the overlap rule: a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap must be at most half of the shorter of the two clips (an overlap IS a transition).
{
"properties": {
"track": {
"description": "Track id (get_project lists them).",
"type": "integer",
"minimum": 0
},
"project": {

"type": "integer",
"description": "Edit INSIDE a nest, by nest id — get_project lists them under nests, and a nest clip's source.project names the one it shows. With it, every id in this call — clips, tracks, actions — is looked up in THAT nest's own tracks and clips instead of the timeline's, and every time is the nest's own, measured from its zero (a nest has no speed, so the whole mapping is t minus the nest clip's start); media ids are unaffected, because a nest shares the document's media. The op itself is unchanged and one call is still one undo step. Omit it to edit whatever the app has OPEN — the timeline, or the nest set_scope entered, exactly as an edit made by hand goes where the window is looking — so this argument is how you act on a container you are not looking at, and get_project always says which one you are in. Eight ops have no meaning inside a nest and refuse by name when you ask for one: add_marker, set_marker, remove_marker, set_canvas, add_media, relink_media, remove_media, add_adjustment_clip. The first seven behave DIFFERENTLY when the scope is inherited from set_scope rather than asked for here, and the result says which: five of them, plus set_marker's name / chapter / color and remove_marker, simply land on the DOCUMENT and are named under document_ops. The two that carry a TIME — add_marker, and set_marker with a time — are refused instead, because a marker is at project time while the playhead inside a nest is not, so the tick you would send means the wrong frame. Leave the nest (set_scope with no arguments) or pass the tick in project time. Probes a movie, sound file or picture and adds it to the project's media list, returning its new media id — File ▸ Add Media…. It is NOT on the timeline yet: place it with add_clip {track, media, at}. The result also reports what the probe found (kind, duration, display size, frame rate, whether it has video, audio or an alpha channel), which is what you need to place and size it. A WebM or Matroska file is copied into a .mov first: the result's path is the copy and its original is the file you named, which the media is named after. A file the opt-in ffmpeg step converts is recorded the same way.

export
Starts writing the timeline to a file and answers AT ONCE with {export_id, path, status} — ⌘E, the export sheet's six controls (format, size, frame rate, quality, loudness, range) in the sheet's own vocabulary, all but the frame rate — this exports at the document's rate, or on gif and apng at the format's own rate (12.5 and 25 fps). The export is a job in the Export Queue, run one at a time behind any other export already there; status is queued or running. An av1, av1_webm or vp9_webm job also waits while the app's other AV1 and VP9 exports would hold more than a quarter of this Mac's memory with it, and a later job may run first meanwhile (export_status's waiting says so). Follow it with export_status, which never waits — call it again after a pause until status is done, failed or cancelled — and stop it with cancel_export. The export_id lasts until Frame Job quits. Every refusal comes back from this call, before anything is queued: a bad argument, a missing folder, and a graphic clip whose module does not compile; a failure while writing comes back from export_status, failed with its reason (a graphic that fails during the export stops it with no file left, naming the graphic and the frame). The preset is the ENCODING only and the size a separate choice defaulting to the document's own, or on gif and apng to the format's cap; the core resolves both into concrete settings (container, codec, size, rate, range) and hands them to the same exporter the sheet uses, so an agent export and a menu export cannot disagree. An existing file at the path is replaced, and the container's extension is added when the path has none. In an HLG project (set_canvas output) hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 and prores_4444 write HLG unless dynamic_range says pq or sdr, and every other video preset writes the project's SDR version. title: "Work inside a nest"
description: "Open a nest to edit its clips in place, find your way back out, and see what stays project-wide while you're inside."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Open a [nest](/editing/nests/) to change the clips inside it without taking the group apart. The nest clip keeps its own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume, which [Un-nest](/editing/nests/) would throw away.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Open Nest', 'Clip ▸ Close Nest']}
  keys={['⌘↓', '⌘↑']}
  where={['Double-click a nest clip', 'The breadcrumb, in the corner above the track headers']}
  tools="set_scope"
/>

## Open a nest

Double-click a nest clip. You can also select one nest clip and choose **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>).

**Clip ▸ Open Nest** needs exactly one nest clip selected, so it's greyed out with two selected. A double-click doesn't mind what else is selected, because it names its own clip.

A nest can hold nests. Open one the same way from inside, down to eight levels.

Because a double-click opens a nest clip, it can't rename one. Use **Clip ▸ Rename…** (<kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>) or the name field in the Clip tab.

## Come back out

Choose **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>), or click the [breadcrumb](#use-the-breadcrumb). Either one goes out one level, and the nest clip you went in through is selected again.

**Clip ▸ Close Nest** is greyed out at the top level. **Open Nest** and **Close Nest** are both greyed out while you're typing in a field, so <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> stay with the text.

## Use the breadcrumb

While a nest is open, the corner above the track headers shows a path such as `Timeline › Intro`, with a back arrow in front of it.

- It shows the last two levels: the one you'd return to, then the one you're in, in bold. Hover over it for the full path.
- A level is named after the nest clip you went in through, so renaming that clip changes the path.
- A long name is shortened in the middle, so `Lower Third 1` and `Lower Third 2` still look different.

Click anywhere in the corner to go out one level, the same as <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. A double-click counts as one click, so to go up two levels, click twice with a pause or press <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> twice.

With no nest open, the corner is empty and does nothing.

## What you see inside

The timeline shows the nest's own tracks and clips, counted from the nest's own zero. That's all of its contents, including anything the nest clip's [trim](/editing/nest-copies/#trim-a-nest-clip) is hiding on the outer timeline.

The canvas shows the nest at its fixed size, without the nest clip's position, scale, opacity or fades, and you hear it without the nest clip's volume. You're editing the group on its own terms, and the nest clip's settings come back when you leave.

## Where the playhead goes

The playhead moves with you, so the frame under it doesn't change. It also carries back out. If a nest clip starts at 10 s and the playhead is at 12 s, you go in at 2 s. Move to 3 s, come out, and you're at 13 s.

That holds while the playhead is over the nest clip. If it's before the clip when you double-click, you go in at the nest's first frame and come out at the clip's start. If it's past the clip's end, or you move past that point inside, the playhead sits on time the nest clip doesn't play, and the canvas inside shows a frame the timeline won't.

Going in or out also stops playback.

## Going in and out isn't an edit

/// A PQ file's HDR10 peak (spec §11 HD-12): `file`, what import read, in
/// whole cd/m², with `from` naming its field (present exactly when `file`
/// is); `peak`, the person's override. Each key is written only when set, so
/// a PQ file whose import read nothing stores `{}` — which still says the
/// media IS a PQ file, the one a peak may be set on.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct PqColor {
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub file: Option<u32>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub from: Option<PeakSource>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub peak: Option<u32>,
}

impl PqColor {
    /// The peak step 0 uses: the override, else the file's; `None` means
    /// the app's 1,000 cd/m².
    pub fn effective(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        self.peak.or(self.file)
    }
}

/// A video media's camera-log setting: a built-in curve and its gamut, or a
/// `lut` media used as the input conversion instead; `detected` is true
/// when import read it from the file's label; `pq` a PQ file's peak (format
/// 22). Each key is written only when set (`detected` only when true), and
/// `media.color` itself only when the media has one, so a project with none
/// writes the text it did before version 19.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct MediaColor {
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub log: Option<LogCurve>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub gamut: Option<CameraGamut>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub lut: Option<u32>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "is_false")]
    pub detected: bool,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub pq: Option<PqColor>,
}

### Using your own LUT

**Use LUT…** opens a file panel asking you to "Choose a .cube LUT that converts this file's log footage to Rec. 709." The LUT is added to the project's media list and becomes this file's conversion, all in one **Camera Log** step. Its output is taken as Rec. 709. Other files can then pick it from the popup as **LUT: *name***. If that LUT is already in the Media list, its entry is reused instead of a second one being added. A file that can't be read as a LUT shows an error.

A LUT that is some file's Camera Log counts as used: **Unused only** hides it, and Remove asks first.

If you remove that LUT from the Media list, the alert says how many files use it as their Camera Log, for example "the Camera Log of 2 files, which lose it". **Remove and Clear Looks** removes it, and those files go back to no conversion.

### Camera Log and looks

Camera Log is applied before any look. If a clip's file is converted by Camera Log and you also give the clip a camera LUT as a look, the Look section warns: "This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice." It is only a warning, because a creative LUT on top is legitimate. See [Colour grading](color-grading.md).

*Agents:* `set_media_color` (`color` is `{log, gamut?}`, `{lut}` or `null`); `get_project`'s `media[].color` shows `detected: true` for a file set at import.

## HDR10 peak

A PQ (HDR10) file has its highlights roll off to white at the brightness its own metadata names. Import reads the peak from the file: MaxCLL first, then the mastering display's maximum. It looks in the file's sample description and, when that names none, in the video stream's own HDR10 metadata (HEVC SEI, or AV1 metadata), so files from ffmpeg, HandBrake or x265 are read too. A file that names no peak is treated as 1,000 cd/m².

The **HDR10** section of the **Media** tab appears once the project has a PQ file. That can be a video, or a PQ still image (PNG, HEIF or AVIF). Click the file in the list to see and change its peak. The section's header shows the selected file's peak in cd/m² (for example "4,000 cd/m²"), so you can read it with the section collapsed.

---
title: "Editing inside a nest"
description: "Open a nest with set_scope or name one on a single call with scope, and see what follows the open nest and what won't work inside one."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A [nest](/editing/nests/) is a group of clips collapsed into one clip, and it has its own tracks, clips and clock. An agent can work inside one in two ways: open it, as you would, or name it on a single call.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Open Nest', 'Clip ▸ Close Nest']}
  keys={['⌘↓', '⌘↑']}
  where="Double-click a nest clip"
  tools="set_scope"
/>

## Choose how to get in

| | Open it with `set_scope` | Name it with `scope` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | A change of view, like double-clicking the nest clip | An argument on one edit tool |
| How long it lasts | Until `set_scope` with no arguments | That one call |
| What it reaches | A nest a clip shows, at any depth | Any nest in the project, shown or not |
| Who it affects | Every later call, and what the window shows | Only that call. The window stays where it is |
| When to use it | You want to look: `get_project`, `render_frame`, or a tool that takes no `scope` | You want one edit, from wherever you are |

Editing doesn't need the nest open. Opening it is how you see what an edit did.

## Open and close a nest with `set_scope`

`set_scope` mirrors double-clicking a nest clip, or **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>). Called with no arguments it comes back out, as **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>) does, but all the way to the timeline in one call.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | No | The nest clip to open. Works at any depth, and is the precise choice. |
| `nest` | integer | No | The nest to open, by id. A clip on the timeline has to show it. |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

Give `clip` or `nest`, never both. Giving neither means the timeline.

**`clip` is the one to prefer.** Two clips can show one nest, and each measures the times inside from its own start, so only the clip says which of them you mean. It finds the clip in the timeline or in any nest, and the call means the same thing wherever you are now, so there's no need to step down one level at a time.

**`nest` looks at the timeline only.** Where two timeline clips show the nest, the earliest is entered, and a tie goes to the lower id. A nest that's shown only from inside another nest can't be reached this way. Name its nest clip with `clip`, or send the edit with `scope`, which needs no view at all.

### While a nest is open

- [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/#the-report-while-a-nest-is-open) reports the nest as if it were the project, and [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) draws it at its own size.
- Every edit lands inside the nest, unless the call has a `scope` of its own or is one of the [document edits](#document-edits-while-a-nest-is-open).
- The playhead, the selection and the range all belong to the nest. Times you send and read are measured from the nest's own zero.

`set_scope` moves the view and edits nothing, so it adds no undo step. The playhead moves with it so the frame under it stays the same, as it does [for you](/editing/inside-a-nest/#where-the-playhead-goes). Every change of nest clears the in and out range. Going in clears the selection, and coming out selects the nest clip you went in through.

If an edit or an undo takes away the nest that's open, Frame Job falls back to the nearest level that still exists.

### What it answers

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | `true`. |
| `scope` | The open nest's id, the number an edit's `scope` takes. `null` at the timeline. |
| `scope_clip` | The nest clip it was entered through. |
| `scope_path` | The trail from the timeline, one `{nest, clip, name}` for each level. |
| `playhead` | The playhead, in the nest's own time. |
| `project` | The project summary. |

`scope_clip` and `scope_path` appear only while a nest is open. `get_project` reports the same three keys.

### When it refuses

| It says | Why |
| --- | --- |
| "Pass nest or clip, not both…" | Both arguments were given. |
| "No clip has id 17, in this timeline or in any of its nests…" | No clip anywhere has that id. |
| "Clip 17 does not show a nest, so there is nothing to open inside it…" | The clip exists but isn't a nest clip. Its `source.kind` isn't `nest`. |
| "no nest with id 4…" | The project has no such nest. |
| "No clip on the timeline shows nest 4, so the view cannot reach it in one step…" | The nest is shown only from inside another nest, or by no clip at all. |

## The `scope` argument

Every edit tool takes an optional `scope`, a nest id, so one call edits inside that nest from wherever the window is looking. It's the same edit and still one undo step.

```json
{ "clips": [41], "at": 1200000, "scope": 4 }
```

Sent to `split`, that cuts clip 41 inside nest 4, at 2 s on the nest's own clock.

To find the id, read `nests` in `get_project`, or the `source.project` of the nest clip that shows it.

With `scope`:

- Every clip, track and action id is looked up in that nest, not on the timeline.
- Every time is the nest's own, measured from its zero. A nest has no speed, so a moment on the timeline is that time less the nest clip's start.
- Media ids don't change, because a nest shares the project's media.
- It outranks any nest that's open. To edit the timeline while a nest is open you can't name the timeline, so call `set_scope` with no arguments first.

Leave `scope` out, or send `null`, to edit whatever is open: the timeline, or the nest `set_scope` entered.

The answer carries `scope`, the nest the edit landed in, so you can tell it from an edit on the timeline. Clips and tracks the edit made are listed in `new_clips` and `new_tracks` wherever they landed. The `project` summary in the same answer counts the timeline's tracks and clips, so it doesn't move when an edit lands in a nest.

### When a `scope` is refused

A `scope` is checked before any other argument, because it decides what the rest of the call means.

| It says | Why |
| --- | --- |
| "no nest with id 4. get_project lists them under nests, and a nest clip's source.project names the one it shows." | The project has no such nest. |
| "scope must be a nest id, not …" | The value isn't a whole number that could be an id. A number written as a string counts as a number here. |
| "No clip has id 17 inside nest 4…" | The id isn't in that nest. The sentence goes on to say how to get back: drop the `scope`, or, when the nest is only open, call `set_scope` with no arguments. Tracks work the same way. |
| "detect_silence does not take scope. It takes …" | The tool isn't an edit tool. See [below](#tools-that-follow-the-open-nest). |

## Tools that follow the open nest

Tools that aren't plain edits take no `scope`, and refuse one by name. They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open, and on the timeline otherwise, so open the nest first to measure or place inside it.

| What it does | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Measure and read | `detect_silence`, `detect_fillers`, `get_timeline_transcript`, `get_media_analysis`, `get_cursor_events` |
| Sound | `normalize_clip`, `enhance_voice`, `match_audio`, `sync_audio` |
| Captions and words | `transcribe`, `transcribe_for_fillers`, `import_captions`, `export_captions`, `relay_captions` |
| Picture and timing | `split_at_shots`, `analyze_cutout`, `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `switch_angle`, `switch_by_speaker` |
| Adding things | `insert_graphic`, which places its clip in the nest, and `record_screen`, which does the same |
| View state | `set_playhead`, `set_range`, `set_selection` |

A tool that takes a while reads the project first and checks it again before it edits. If the project or the open nest changed meanwhile, it stops and changes nothing, and says to call it again.

Three tools work on the top-level timeline only. With a nest open they refuse, saying to call `set_scope` with no nest first:

- `text_behind_subject`
- `new_project_from_range`
- `make_vertical_version`

Two go on acting on the whole project whatever is open. `export` always writes the whole timeline, and `save_project` saves the whole project.

## `protected_nests` in `detect_silence`

[Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) never cuts into a nest, so a quiet stretch that runs across one is left alone. `detect_silence` names those nest clips under `protected_nests`, because there may be dead air inside them.

<Steps>

1. Call `detect_silence`. Read `protected_nests`, a list of nest clip ids.

2. Call `set_scope` with `clip` set to one of those ids.

3. Call `detect_silence` again. It now measures inside the nest, and its times are the nest's own.

4. Pass the ranges to `ripple_delete_ranges`, which lands in the open nest. Like any edit tool it also takes `scope`.

5. Call `set_scope` with no arguments to come back out.

</Steps>

## What doesn't work inside a nest

Some edits are about the whole project, so a nest has nothing for them to change. What happens depends on whether the nest was named with `scope` or is only open.

| Edit | With `scope` | With the nest only open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add_marker` | Refused | Refused |
| `set_marker` with a `time` | Refused | Refused |
| `set_marker` without a `time` | Refused | Lands on the project |
| `remove_marker` | Refused | Lands on the project |
| `set_canvas` | Refused | Lands on the project |
| `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media` | Refused | Land on the project |
| `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech`, `set_media_cursor` | Refused | Land on the project |
| `add_adjustment_clip` | Refused | Refused |
| `set_track` with `compressor` or `limiter` | Refused | Refused |

### Edit tools refused with a scope

Eleven tools have no meaning inside a nest and refuse a `scope` by name, for example "add_marker has no meaning inside nest 4".

| Tools | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `add_marker`, `set_marker`, `remove_marker` | A nest has no markers. Markers are project time, and they become chapters in the exported file. |
| `set_canvas` | The frame rate and background are the project's, and a nest's size was fixed when it was made. |
| `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech`, `set_media_cursor` | A nest shares the project's one media list. |
| `add_adjustment_clip` | An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) grades what's behind it on the timeline only. This one is refused with a nest open too. |

`set_track` works inside a nest, except that a track's `compressor` and `limiter` are refused, with or without `scope`: a track's dynamics run on the timeline's own mix. A nest's whole sound goes through the track holding its nest clip, so set them there. Volume, pan and the rest of `set_track` mean the same inside a nest as outside.

### Document edits while a nest is open

When a nest is only open, and the call has no `scope`, ten of those tools apply to the whole project, because that's what they're about. It's the same as you choosing **File ▸ Add Media…** with a nest open.

Those are `set_marker` without a `time`, `remove_marker`, `set_canvas`, `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech` and `set_media_cursor`.

The answer lists what went to the project under `document_ops`, and leaves `scope` out because nothing landed in the nest:

```json
{ "ok": true, "document_ops": ["set_canvas"], "project": { … } }
```

`import_media` adds to the project in the same way, with a nest open or not. It has its own answer, with no `document_ops`.

### Markers refused while a nest is open

`add_marker`, and `set_marker` with a `time`, are refused while a nest is open, whatever time you send. A marker sits at project time, and every tick in the call is measured from the nest's own zero, so the marker would land somewhere else on the timeline. It's the reason **Mark ▸ Add Marker** is greyed out in there.

Leave the nest with `set_scope` and no arguments, then send the time in project ticks. A marker's name, chapter setting and colour mean the same in either place, so `set_marker` still changes those. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/#good-to-know).

### Document-wide limits inside a nest

An edit can be valid inside the nest and still be refused for the project's sake, because these limits count every nest and the timeline together:

| Limit | Counted over |
| --- | --- |
| 4,096 clips | The timeline and every nest |
| 64 tracks | The timeline and every nest |
| 8 levels of nesting | The deepest chain of nests |

So read the answer rather than assuming the edit landed. A refusal names the limit, for example "too many tracks: 65 (max 64)".

## Related

- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
- [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/)
- [Read the project: get_project](/mcp/get-project/)
- [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/)
- [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/)

| "no nest with id 4. get_project lists them under nests, and a nest clip's source.project names the one it shows." | The project has no such nest. |
| "scope must be a nest id, not …" | The value isn't a whole number that could be an id. A number written as a string counts as a number here. |
| "No clip has id 17 inside nest 4…" | The id isn't in that nest. The sentence goes on to say how to get back: drop the `scope`, or, when the nest is only open, call `set_scope` with no arguments. Tracks work the same way. |
| "detect_silence does not take scope. It takes …" | The tool isn't an edit tool. See [below](#tools-that-follow-the-open-nest). |

## Tools that follow the open nest

Tools that aren't plain edits take no `scope`, and refuse one by name. They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open, and on the timeline otherwise, so open the nest first to measure or place inside it.

| What it does | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Measure and read | `detect_silence`, `detect_fillers`, `get_timeline_transcript`, `get_media_analysis`, `get_cursor_events` |
| Sound | `normalize_clip`, `enhance_voice`, `match_audio`, `sync_audio` |
| Captions and words | `transcribe`, `transcribe_for_fillers`, `import_captions`, `export_captions`, `relay_captions` |
| Picture and timing | `split_at_shots`, `analyze_cutout`, `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `switch_angle`, `switch_by_speaker` |
| Adding things | `insert_graphic`, which places its clip in the nest, and `record_screen`, which does the same |
| View state | `set_playhead`, `set_range`, `set_selection` |

A tool that takes a while reads the project first and checks it again before it edits. If the project or the open nest changed meanwhile, it stops and changes nothing, and says to call it again.

Three tools work on the top-level timeline only. With a nest open they refuse, saying to call `set_scope` with no nest first:

- `text_behind_subject`
- `new_project_from_range`
- `make_vertical_version`

Two go on acting on the whole project whatever is open. `export` always writes the whole timeline, and `save_project` saves the whole project.

## `protected_nests` in `detect_silence`

[Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) never cuts into a nest, so a quiet stretch that runs across one is left alone. `detect_silence` names those nest clips under `protected_nests`, because there may be dead air inside them.

<Steps>

1. Call `detect_silence`. Read `protected_nests`, a list of nest clip ids.

2. Call `set_scope` with `clip` set to one of those ids.

3. Call `detect_silence` again. It now measures inside the nest, and its times are the nest's own.

4. Pass the ranges to `ripple_delete_ranges`, which lands in the open nest. Like any edit tool it also takes `scope`.

5. Call `set_scope` with no arguments to come back out.

</Steps>

## What doesn't work inside a nest

Some edits are about the whole project, so a nest has nothing for them to change. What happens depends on whether the nest was named with `scope` or is only open.

| Edit | With `scope` | With the nest only open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add_marker` | Refused | Refused |
| `set_marker` with a `time` | Refused | Refused |
| `set_marker` without a `time` | Refused | Lands on the project |
| `remove_marker` | Refused | Lands on the project |
| `set_canvas` | Refused | Lands on the project |
| `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media` | Refused | Land on the project |
| `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech`, `set_media_cursor` | Refused | Land on the project |
| `add_adjustment_clip` | Refused | Refused |
| `set_track` with `compressor` or `limiter` | Refused | Refused |

### Edit tools refused with a scope

Eleven tools have no meaning inside a nest and refuse a `scope` by name, for example "add_marker has no meaning inside nest 4".

| Tools | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `add_marker`, `set_marker`, `remove_marker` | A nest has no markers. Markers are project time, and they become chapters in the exported file. |
| `set_canvas` | The frame rate and background are the project's, and a nest's size was fixed when it was made. |
| `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech`, `set_media_cursor` | A nest shares the project's one media list. |
| `add_adjustment_clip` | An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) grades what's behind it on the timeline only. This one is refused with a nest open too. |

`set_track` works inside a nest, except that a track's `compressor` and `limiter` are refused, with or without `scope`: a track's dynamics run on the timeline's own mix. A nest's whole sound goes through the track holding its nest clip, so set them there. Volume, pan and the rest of `set_track` mean the same inside a nest as outside.

### Document edits while a nest is open

When a nest is only open, and the call has no `scope`, ten of those tools apply to the whole project, because that's what they're about. It's the same as you choosing **File ▸ Add Media…** with a nest open.

Those are `set_marker` without a `time`, `remove_marker`, `set_canvas`, `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech` and `set_media_cursor`.

The answer lists what went to the project under `document_ops`, and leaves `scope` out because nothing landed in the nest:

```json
{ "ok": true, "document_ops": ["set_canvas"], "project": { … } }
```

`import_media` adds to the project in the same way, with a nest open or not. It has its own answer, with no `document_ops`.

### Markers refused while a nest is open

`add_marker`, and `set_marker` with a `time`, are refused while a nest is open, whatever time you send. A marker sits at project time, and every tick in the call is measured from the nest's own zero, so the marker would land somewhere else on the timeline. It's the reason **Mark ▸ Add Marker** is greyed out in there.

Leave the nest with `set_scope` and no arguments, then send the time in project ticks. A marker's name, chapter setting and colour mean the same in either place, so `set_marker` still changes those. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/#good-to-know).

### Document-wide limits inside a nest

An edit can be valid inside the nest and still be refused for the project's sake, because these limits count every nest and the timeline together:

| Limit | Counted over |
| --- | --- |
| 4,096 clips | The timeline and every nest |
| 64 tracks | The timeline and every nest |
| 8 levels of nesting | The deepest chain of nests |

So read the answer rather than assuming the edit landed. A refusal names the limit, for example "too many tracks: 65 (max 64)".

## Related

- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
- [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/)
- [Read the project: get_project](/mcp/get-project/)
- [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/)
- [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: "Editing inside a nest"
description: "Open a nest with set_scope or name one on a single call with scope, and see what follows the open nest and what won't work inside one."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A [nest](/editing/nests/) is a group of clips collapsed into one clip, and it has its own tracks, clips and clock. An agent can work inside one in two ways: open it, as you would, or name it on a single call.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Open Nest', 'Clip ▸ Close Nest']}
  keys={['⌘↓', '⌘↑']}
  where="Double-click a nest clip"
  tools="set_scope"
/>

## Choose how to get in

| | Open it with `set_scope` | Name it with `scope` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | A change of view, like double-clicking the nest clip | An argument on one edit tool |
| How long it lasts | Until `set_scope` with no arguments | That one call |
| What it reaches | A nest a clip shows, at any depth | Any nest in the project, shown or not |
| Who it affects | Every later call, and what the window shows | Only that call. The window stays where it is |
| When to use it | You want to look: `get_project`, `render_frame`, or a tool that takes no `scope` | You want one edit, from wherever you are |

Editing doesn't need the nest open. Opening it is how you see what an edit did.

## Open and close a nest with `set_scope`

`set_scope` mirrors double-clicking a nest clip, or **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>). Called with no arguments it comes back out, as **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>) does, but all the way to the timeline in one call.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | No | The nest clip to open. Works at any depth, and is the precise choice. |
| `nest` | integer | No | The nest to open, by id. A clip on the timeline has to show it. |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

Give `clip` or `nest`, never both. Giving neither means the timeline.

**`clip` is the one to prefer.** Two clips can show one nest, and each measures the times inside from its own start, so only the clip says which of them you mean. It finds the clip in the timeline or in any nest, and the call means the same thing wherever you are now, so there's no need to step down one level at a time.

**`nest` looks at the timeline only.** Where two timeline clips show the nest, the earliest is entered, and a tie goes to the lower id. A nest that's shown only from inside another nest can't be reached this way. Name its nest clip with `clip`, or send the edit with `scope`, which needs no view at all.

### While a nest is open

- [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/#the-report-while-a-nest-is-open) reports the nest as if it were the project, and [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) draws it at its own size.
- Every edit lands inside the nest, unless the call has a `scope` of its own or is one of the [document edits](#document-edits-while-a-nest-is-open).
- The playhead, the selection and the range all belong to the nest. Times you send and read are measured from the nest's own zero.

`set_scope` moves the view and edits nothing, so it adds no undo step. The playhead moves with it so the frame under it stays the same, as it does [for you](/editing/inside-a-nest/#where-the-playhead-goes). Every change of nest clears the in and out range. Going in clears the selection, and coming out selects the nest clip you went in through.

If an edit or an undo takes away the nest that's open, Frame Job falls back to the nearest level that still exists.

### What it answers

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | `true`. |
| `scope` | The open nest's id, the number an edit's `scope` takes. `null` at the timeline. |
| `scope_clip` | The nest clip it was entered through. |
| `scope_path` | The trail from the timeline, one `{nest, clip, name}` for each level. |
| `playhead` | The playhead, in the nest's own time. |
| `project` | The project summary. |

`scope_clip` and `scope_path` appear only while a nest is open. `get_project` reports the same three keys.

### When it refuses

| It says | Why |
| --- | --- |
| "Pass nest or clip, not both…" | Both arguments were given. |
| "No clip has id 17, in this timeline or in any of its nests…" | No clip anywhere has that id. |
| "Clip 17 does not show a nest, so there is nothing to open inside it…" | The clip exists but isn't a nest clip. Its `source.kind` isn't `nest`. |
| "no nest with id 4…" | The project has no such nest. |
| "No clip on the timeline shows nest 4, so the view cannot reach it in one step…" | The nest is shown only from inside another nest, or by no clip at all. |

## The `scope` argument

Every edit tool takes an optional `scope`, a nest id, so one call edits inside that nest from wherever the window is looking. It's the same edit and still one undo step.

```json
{ "clips": [41], "at": 1200000, "scope": 4 }
```

Sent to `split`, that cuts clip 41 inside nest 4, at 2 s on the nest's own clock.

To find the id, read `nests` in `get_project`, or the `source.project` of the nest clip that shows it.

With `scope`:

- Every clip, track and action id is looked up in that nest, not on the timeline.
- Every time is the nest's own, measured from its zero. A nest has no speed, so a moment on the timeline is that time less the nest clip's start.
- Media ids don't change, because a nest shares the project's media.
- It outranks any nest that's open. To edit the timeline while a nest is open you can't name the timeline, so call `set_scope` with no arguments first.

Leave `scope` out, or send `null`, to edit whatever is open: the timeline, or the nest `set_scope` entered.

The answer carries `scope`, the nest the edit landed in, so you can tell it from an edit on the timeline. Clips and tracks the edit made are listed in `new_clips` and `new_tracks` wherever they landed. The `project` summary in the same answer counts the timeline's tracks and clips, so it doesn't move when an edit lands in a nest.

### When a `scope` is refused

A `scope` is checked before any other argument, because it decides what the rest of the call means.

| It says | Why |
| --- | --- |
| "no nest with id 4. get_project lists them under nests, and a nest clip's source.project names the one it shows." | The project has no such nest. |
| "scope must be a nest id, not …" | The value isn't a whole number that could be an id. A number written as a string counts as a number here. |
| "No clip has id 17 inside nest 4…" | The id isn't in that nest. The sentence goes on to say how to get back: drop the `scope`, or, when the nest is only open, call `set_scope` with no arguments. Tracks work the same way. |
| "detect_silence does not take scope. It takes …" | The tool isn't an edit tool. See [below](#tools-that-follow-the-open-nest). |

## Tools that follow the open nest

Tools that aren't plain edits take no `scope`, and refuse one by name. They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open, and on the timeline otherwise, so open the nest first to measure or place inside it.

| What it does | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Measure and read | `detect_silence`, `detect_fillers`, `get_timeline_transcript`, `get_media_analysis`, `get_cursor_events` |
| Sound | `normalize_clip`, `enhance_voice`, `match_audio`, `sync_audio` |
| Captions and words | `transcribe`, `transcribe_for_fillers`, `import_captions`, `export_captions`, `relay_captions` |
| Picture and timing | `split_at_shots`, `analyze_cutout`, `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `switch_angle`, `switch_by_speaker` |
| Adding things | `insert_graphic`, which places its clip in the nest, and `record_screen`, which does the same |
| View state | `set_playhead`, `set_range`, `set_selection` |

A tool that takes a while reads the project first and checks it again before it edits. If the project or the open nest changed meanwhile, it stops and changes nothing, and says to call it again.

Three tools work on the top-level timeline only. With a nest open they refuse, saying to call `set_scope` with no nest first:

- `text_behind_subject`
- `new_project_from_range`
- `make_vertical_version`

Two go on acting on the whole project whatever is open. `export` always writes the whole timeline, and `save_project` saves the whole project.

## `protected_nests` in `detect_silence`

[Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) never cuts into a nest, so a quiet stretch that runs across one is left alone. `detect_silence` names those nest clips under `protected_nests`, because there may be dead air inside them.

<Steps>

1. Call `detect_silence`. Read `protected_nests`, a list of nest clip ids.

2. Call `set_scope` with `clip` set to one of those ids.

3. Call `detect_silence` again. It now measures inside the nest, and its times are the nest's own.

4. Pass the ranges to `ripple_delete_ranges`, which lands in the open nest. Like any edit tool it also takes `scope`.

5. Call `set_scope` with no arguments to come back out.

</Steps>

## What doesn't work inside a nest

Some edits are about the whole project, so a nest has nothing for them to change. What happens depends on whether the nest was named with `scope` or is only open.

| Edit | With `scope` | With the nest only open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add_marker` | Refused | Refused |
| `set_marker` with a `time` | Refused | Refused |
| `set_marker` without a `time` | Refused | Lands on the project |
| `remove_marker` | Refused | Lands on the project |
| `set_canvas` | Refused | Lands on the project |
| `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media` | Refused | Land on the project |
| `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech`, `set_media_cursor` | Refused | Land on the project |
| `add_adjustment_clip` | Refused | Refused |
| `set_track` with `compressor` or `limiter` | Refused | Refused |

### Edit tools refused with a scope

Eleven tools have no meaning inside a nest and refuse a `scope` by name, for example "add_marker has no meaning inside nest 4".

| Tools | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `add_marker`, `set_marker`, `remove_marker` | A nest has no markers. Markers are project time, and they become chapters in the exported file. |
| `set_canvas` | The frame rate and background are the project's, and a nest's size was fixed when it was made. |
| `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech`, `set_media_cursor` | A nest shares the project's one media list. |
| `add_adjustment_clip` | An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) grades what's behind it on the timeline only. This one is refused with a nest open too. |

`set_track` works inside a nest, except that a track's `compressor` and `limiter` are refused, with or without `scope`: a track's dynamics run on the timeline's own mix. A nest's whole sound goes through the track holding its nest clip, so set them there. Volume, pan and the rest of `set_track` mean the same inside a nest as outside.

### Document edits while a nest is open

When a nest is only open, and the call has no `scope`, ten of those tools apply to the whole project, because that's what they're about. It's the same as you choosing **File ▸ Add Media…** with a nest open.

Those are `set_marker` without a `time`, `remove_marker`, `set_canvas`, `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech` and `set_media_cursor`.

The answer lists what went to the project under `document_ops`, and leaves `scope` out because nothing landed in the nest:

```json
{ "ok": true, "document_ops": ["set_canvas"], "project": { … } }
```

`import_media` adds to the project in the same way, with a nest open or not. It has its own answer, with no `document_ops`.

### Markers refused while a nest is open

`add_marker`, and `set_marker` with a `time`, are refused while a nest is open, whatever time you send. A marker sits at project time, and every tick in the call is measured from the nest's own zero, so the marker would land somewhere else on the timeline. It's the reason **Mark ▸ Add Marker** is greyed out in there.

Leave the nest with `set_scope` and no arguments, then send the time in project ticks. A marker's name, chapter setting and colour mean the same in either place, so `set_marker` still changes those. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/#good-to-know).

### Document-wide limits inside a nest

An edit can be valid inside the nest and still be refused for the project's sake, because these limits count every nest and the timeline together:

| Limit | Counted over |
| --- | --- |
| 4,096 clips | The timeline and every nest |
| 64 tracks | The timeline and every nest |
| 8 levels of nesting | The deepest chain of nests |

So read the answer rather than assuming the edit landed. A refusal names the limit, for example "too many tracks: 65 (max 64)".

## Related

- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
- [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/)
- [Read the project: get_project](/mcp/get-project/)
- [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/)
- [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/)

Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>
